root.description:
Stops the upward search for configuration files: no file above this one contributes. Only valid in a file
found by discovery, not in one reached through `extends`.

extends.description: Configuration files to inherit, relative to this file. They apply before this file does, in the order listed.

reset.description: Inherited lists to discard before this file applies.

workspace.description: `[workspace]`: package-manager detection and which packages are skipped.

rules.description: `[rules]`: the level and options of every configured rule, in file order.

version-groups.description: `[[version-groups]]`: how dependency versions must relate, first match wins.

semver-groups.description: `[[semver-groups]]`: the range type dependencies must use, first match wins.

custom-types.description: `[[custom-types]]`: manifest fields that hold versions and take part in the version policies.

catalog.description: `[catalog]`: when catalog entries are suggested and reported.

workspace-protocol.description: `[workspace-protocol]`: how dependencies on workspace packages are written.

dependency-families.description: `[[dependency-families]]`: packages that must share a version.

update.description: `[update]`: how `skif update` reads the package registry. Linting never reads it.

update-groups.description: `[[update-groups]]`: how far `skif update` may move the dependencies it matches, first match wins.

format.description: `[format]`: how `package-json-format` and `skif format` order and lay out `package.json` files.

overrides.description: Scoped rules for packages and files; only package-scoped keys are allowed in them.

oneOf.description: Discard the inherited `version-groups`.
Discard the inherited `semver-groups`.
Discard the inherited `ignore` entries.
Discard the inherited `dependency-families`.
Discard the inherited `custom-types`.
Discard the inherited `overrides`.
Discard the inherited `update-groups`.

ResetKey.description: The inherited lists that `reset` can discard.

ignore-packages.description: Package names or globs excluded from every check.

discover-ignore.description:
Gitignore-style patterns, relative to the directory a recursive run starts in, of directories that root
discovery (`-r`) does not enter, so no project below them is found. A bare name matches at any depth; a
pattern with a slash is anchored at the start directory. Replaces the default list
(`__fixtures__`, `fixtures`, `__mocks__`, `__snapshots__`); `[]` skips nothing. Read from the configuration
file that governs the start directory.

extend-ignore-packages.description: Appended to `ignore-packages` instead of replacing it. Folded away when the configuration is resolved.

oneOf.description: npm.
pnpm.
Yarn.
Bun.

PackageManager.description: Package managers that can be forced with `[workspace] package-manager`.

fail-on-warnings.description: Exit non-zero when only warnings were reported.

max-level.description: Caps the severity of every diagnostic: a rule configured above this level reports at it.

oneOf.description: The rule does not run.
Diagnostics are informational.
Diagnostics are warnings.
Diagnostics are errors.

Level.description: The level a rule is configured to: `off`, `info`, `warn` or `error`.

RuleConfigSchema.description:
Schema stand-in for a `[rules]` value: a level string or a table of `level` plus options.
It only describes the shape for the JSON Schema and is never constructed.

level.description: The level of the rule; the key that is written back. Set either `level` or `severity`, not both.

RuleTableSchema.description: Table form of a rule entry; the options present depend on the rule.

rules.description: Rule IDs to suppress; an empty list does not narrow the entry by rule.

packages.description: Package names or directories; an empty selector matches every package.

dependencies.description: Dependency names; an empty selector matches every dependency.

reason.description: Why the suppression exists. `--require-ignore-reasons` fails a run on an entry without one.

IgnoreEntry.description:
One `[[ignore]]` suppression. An empty list does not narrow that dimension, but at least one list must be set:
an entry without any filter is rejected as it would suppress everything.

dependency-types.description: Dependency types the policy rules apply to. Empty means production and development dependencies (`dependencies` and `devDependencies`); name `peer` or `optional` to include them.

override-reading.description:
How `resolutions`, `overrides` and `pnpm-overrides` entries become dependency instances: `skif` (default) names
the package a selector replaces, `syncpack` reads them as syncpack 15 does.

oneOf.description: Prefer the highest version in use.
Prefer the lowest version in use.

The dependency of an entry is the package its selector replaces (`parent>child` and `child@<2` are `child`),
npm's nested objects are read, and `pnpm.overrides` of every `package.json` is read.

As syncpack 15 reads them: the key of an entry is the dependency name, so `parent>child` and `child@<2` are
dependencies of their own; only string values count (nested objects are skipped); and `pnpm-overrides` is the
`overrides` of `pnpm-workspace.yaml` only.

OverrideReading.description: How the override sections (`resolutions`, `overrides`, `pnpm-overrides`) are read as dependency instances.

dependencies.description: Dependency names the group covers; empty covers every dependency.

packages.description: Package names the group covers; empty covers every package.

dependency-types.description: Dependency types the group covers; empty covers the types `[policy] dependency-types` governs (production and development dependencies and a package's own version by default). Peer and optional dependencies, the override sections and custom types are covered only when named.

specifier-types.description: Specifier types the group covers (`exact`, `range`, `tag`, ...), optionally negated with `!`; empty covers every type.

snap-to.description: Required by `snapped-to`: packages whose version the group follows.

VersionGroup.description: One `[[version-groups]]` entry; first match wins. Selectors accept `!` negation and `$LOCAL`.

oneOf.description: Every matched dependency must use the `pin` version.
The matched dependencies must not be used.
The matched dependencies are not checked.
Every range must overlap every other range.
Every matched dependency must share a major and minor version.
Versions must match those declared by the `snap-to` packages.
Versions must match the highest or lowest one in use.
Versions may differ; only the range the semver groups require is checked (syncpack's `semverRangeOnly`).

VersionPolicy.description: The policy of a version group.

dependencies.description: Dependency names the group covers; empty covers every dependency.

packages.description: Package names the group covers; empty covers every package.

dependency-types.description: Dependency types the group covers; empty covers the types `[policy] dependency-types` governs (production and development dependencies and a package's own version by default). Peer and optional dependencies, the override sections and custom types are covered only when named.

specifier-types.description: Specifier types the group covers, optionally negated with `!`; empty covers every type.

range.description: The range type the matched dependencies must use. Required unless `ignored` is set.

ignored.description:
The matched dependencies have no range requirement and no later semver group applies to them. Exclusive with
`range`.

SemverGroup.description:
One `[[semver-groups]]` entry; first match wins. Set `range`, or `ignored = true` to leave the matched dependencies
without a range requirement (syncpack's `isIgnored` and `isDisabled`).

oneOf.description: No range operator: an exact version.
Any version (`*`).
Compatible versions (`^`).
Patch-level changes (`~`).
Greater than (`>`).
Greater than or equal (`>=`).
Less than (`<`).
Less than or equal (`<=`).

SemverRange.description: The range type a semver group enforces.

name.description:
The token that selects this type in `dependency-types`. It must not be the name of a built-in type
(`prod`, `dev`, `peer`, `optional`, `local`, `resolutions`, `overrides`, `pnpm-overrides`). With the `version`
strategy it is also the dependency name.

path.description: Dotted path of the field in `package.json`, e.g. `engines.node` or `packageManager`.

strategy.description: How the value at `path` holds versions.

name-path.description: With the `name~version` strategy: dotted path of the field that holds the dependency name.

CustomType.description:
One `[[custom-types]]` entry: a field of `package.json` that holds versions. Name it in a `dependency-types` list to
select its instances, like a dependency section (syncpack's `customTypes`).

oneOf.description: The value is a string `name@version` (`"packageManager": "pnpm@9.0.0"`): the dependency is the name.
The value is a version string (`engines.node`): the dependency is named after the custom type.
The value is an object of `name: version` (`pnpm.peerDependencyRules.allowedVersions`).

The value is a version string and the dependency name is the string at `name-path` (how syncpack reads a
package's own `name` and `version`).

CustomStrategy.description: How a [`CustomType`] reads versions from its `path`.

min-packages.description: Minimum number of packages using a dependency before a catalog entry is suggested.

exclude.description: Dependencies never suggested for a catalog.

report-unused-entries.description: Report catalog entries no package references.

extend-exclude.description: Appended to `exclude` instead of replacing it. Folded away when the configuration is resolved.

oneOf.description: Catalog rules suggest nothing.
Suggest moving shared dependencies into a catalog.
Require shared dependencies to come from a catalog.

internal.description: Require `workspace:` for dependencies on other workspace packages.

name.description: The family name; a built-in family of the same name is replaced.

packages.description: Package names or globs that must share a version.

enabled.description: `false` disables a built-in family of the same name.

DependencyFamily.description: One `[[dependency-families]]` entry: packages that must share a version.

minimum-release-age.description:
Minutes a version must have been published before `skif update` proposes it; `0` turns the delay off. Unset,
the `minimumReleaseAge` of `pnpm-workspace.yaml` applies, else one day (1440), as in syncpack.

max-concurrent-requests.description: How many registry requests run at once.

Update.description: `[update]`: how `skif update` reads the package registry (ADR 0058). Linting never reads it.

dependencies.description: Dependency names the group covers; empty covers every dependency.

packages.description:
Package names the group covers; empty covers every package. A group that names packages does not cover catalog
entries, which belong to no package.

dependency-types.description:
Dependency types the group covers; empty covers the types `[policy] dependency-types` governs. A group that
names types does not cover catalog entries.

specifier-types.description: Specifier types the group covers, optionally negated with `!`; empty covers every type.

target.description:
The furthest the matched dependencies may move; combined with `--target`, the stricter wins. Required unless
`ignored` is set.

ignored.description: `skif update` never changes the matched dependencies. Exclusive with `target`.

UpdateGroup.description:
One `[[update-groups]]` entry; first match wins. Set `target` to cap how far `skif update` moves the matched
dependencies, or `ignored = true` to leave them alone (syncpack's `updateGroups`).

oneOf.description: The highest published version, across majors.
The highest version with the same major.
The highest version with the same major and minor.

UpdateTarget.description: How far `skif update` may move a version: syncpack's `--target` and an update group's `target`.

entry.description: Entry-point globs, added to the ones plugins and `package.json` provide.

project.description: Globs of the files that belong to the project.

ignore.description: Globs of files that are not analysed.

ignore-files.description:
Globs of files, relative to the workspace root, never reported by `unused-files`; other rules still analyse
them (knip's `ignoreFiles`).

ignore-dependencies.description: Dependencies never reported as unused or unlisted.

ignore-global-binaries.description:
Never report the system and shell tools scripts run (`rm`, `curl`, `git`, `docker`) as unlisted binaries,
since they are installed globally rather than from npm (knip's `ignoreGlobalBinaries`). On by default; turn it
off to have `unlisted-binaries` report them unless a dependency provides them.

ignore-unresolved.description:
Import specifiers never reported as unresolved. Entries are exact specifiers, globs or regular expressions
(`/^@org\/.+$/`), see the `[js]` documentation.

ignore-workspaces.description: Workspace directories (globs) the JavaScript analysis skips. Manifest and policy rules still check them.

ignore-exports-used-in-file.description: Exports that other code in the same file uses are not reported: `true` for every kind, or a table of kinds.

ignore-members.description: Enum and namespace member names (globs or regular expressions) never reported as unused.

include-entry-exports.description: Report unused exports of entry files too.

tsconfig.description:
The TypeScript configuration of the root package, relative to the workspace root and inside it, used instead
of `tsconfig.json` for its path aliases and compiler options (knip's `--tsConfig`). Other packages keep their
own `tsconfig.json`.

use-tsconfig-files.description:
The project files of a package with a TypeScript configuration are the files its `files` names and those its
`include` selects minus its `exclude`, instead of the `project` globs (knip's `--use-tsconfig-files`).

include-fixtures.description:
Report files in `fixtures` and `__fixtures__` directories as unused, and their unused exports, types and
members, like any other file. Off by default: those directories hold test data that tests load by path.

discovery.description:
How source files are found: `auto` lists them from the git index and re-lists from disk every directory
modified since the index was written, which gives the walk's result without walking every directory; `git`
trusts the index alone (faster, blind to untracked and deleted files); `walk` always walks. Both index modes
fall back to the walk when the workspace is not in a git work tree with a usable SHA-1 index.

workspaces.description: Per-workspace overrides keyed by directory. The key `"."` is the root workspace.

plugins.description: Plugin switches keyed by plugin name.

extend-ignore.description: Appended to `ignore` instead of replacing it. Folded away when the configuration is resolved.

extend-ignore-dependencies.description: Appended to `ignore-dependencies` instead of replacing it. Folded away when the configuration is resolved.

extend-ignore-binaries.description: Appended to `ignore-binaries` instead of replacing it. Folded away when the configuration is resolved.

extend-ignore-unresolved.description: Appended to `ignore-unresolved` instead of replacing it. Folded away when the configuration is resolved.

anyOf.description: `true` ignores every kind of export, `false` none.

IgnoreExportsUsedInFile.description:
`ignore-exports-used-in-file`: `true`, or a table naming the kinds of export it applies to.

It is read by hand rather than as an untagged enum, so that a mistyped kind is reported by name (`unknown field
"fucntion"`) instead of serde's "data did not match any variant".

type.description: Type alias exports. skif does not tell type aliases from interfaces, so this and `interface` are the same.

member.description:
Enum and namespace members. skif always counts a member read in its own file as used, so this key is
accepted for compatibility and has no further effect.

ExportKinds.description: The kinds of export `ignore-exports-used-in-file` can name, as in knip.

oneOf.description:
The git index, checked against the file system: a directory modified since the index was written is listed
from disk, so untracked and deleted files are found as the walk finds them. The directory walk when the
workspace is not in a git work tree with a usable index.

The git index alone, without checking the file system: faster, but blind to files created or deleted since the
last `git add`. The directory walk when there is no usable index.
Always walk the directories.

allow.description:
Cycles that are not reported, each the list of its files relative to the workspace root. A cycle is allowed
when its files are exactly the files of one entry, in any order.

dynamic-imports.description:
Count dynamic `import()` as an edge of a cycle. Off by default: a dynamic import runs after the module graph
is loaded, so it cannot cause an initialisation-order problem.

entry.description: Entry-point globs relative to the workspace directory.

project.description: Project file globs relative to the workspace directory.

ignore.description: Globs of files that are not analysed.

ignore-files.description: Globs of files, relative to the workspace directory, never reported by `unused-files`.

ignore-dependencies.description: Dependencies never reported as unused or unlisted.

ignore-unresolved.description: Import specifiers never reported as unresolved in this workspace.

include-entry-exports.description: Report unused exports of entry files of this workspace; unset inherits `[js] include-entry-exports`.

ignore-exports-used-in-file.description: Exports used in their own file that are not reported in this workspace; unset inherits `[js]`.

ignore-members.description: Enum and namespace member names never reported as unused in this workspace.

paths.description: Module aliases as in a `tsconfig` `paths` map: `{ "alias/*" = ["./target/*"] }`, targets relative to the workspace.

plugins.description: Plugin switches and options for this workspace, applied over `[js.plugins]`.

anyOf.description: A bare switch: `true` forces the plugin on, `false` off.

enabled.description: Forces the plugin on or off; unset keeps its detection.

project.description: Project file globs the plugin contributes.

PluginOptions.description: Table form of a plugin entry.

sort-first.description: Top-level keys that come first, in this order.

sort-az.description:
Fields sorted alphabetically one level deep: an object by key, an array of strings by value. `a/b` names a
nested field. For fields whose order means nothing: an array with a `!`-prefixed entry keeps its order.

sort-exports.description:
Keys that come first, in this order, in every object of `exports`; `default` is always last. The default moves
only `types` and `default`; a key that reorders other conditions makes the fix unsafe.

sort-packages.description: Sort the top-level keys `sort-first` does not name.

format-bugs.description: Write a `bugs` object that holds only `url` as that string.

format-repository.description: Write a `repository` object that holds only `url` and a `type` of `git` (or no `type`) as its shorthand.

indent.description:
Check the layout against `JSON.stringify(manifest, null, indent)`: spaces or tabs, for example `"  "` or
`"\t"`. Unset keeps each file's layout.

Format.description: `[format]`: what the `package-json-format` rule and `skif format` check, with syncpack's defaults (ADR 0055).

packages.description: Package names, or directories (`./apps/old/**`). At least one of `packages` and `files` must be set.

files.description: File globs. When both lists are set, a diagnostic must match both.

max-level.description: Caps the severity of every matched diagnostic.

rules.description: Rule levels; options are root-scoped and not allowed here.

ignore.description: Suppressions limited to the selected packages and files; an entry may omit every filter.

js.description: JavaScript inputs for the selected packages; needs `packages` and no `files`.

Override.description:
One `[[overrides]]` entry: settings for the packages and files it selects.

Patterns are anchored at the directory of the file that declares them: a package pattern starting with `./` is a
directory below it, any other is a package name (or a `$LOCAL`-style token); a file pattern is always a path
below it. A `$ROOT/` prefix anchors a pattern at the root being linted instead, and a path that would leave the
anchor never matches.

Only package-scoped keys are allowed. An override never changes what a workspace-wide analysis computes; it
changes how the diagnostics located in the selected packages or files are reported, and the JavaScript inputs of
the selected packages.

entry.description: Replaces the entry globs; an empty list clears what the package inherits.

project.description: Replaces the project globs; an empty list clears what the package inherits.

ignore.description: Replaces the ignore globs; an empty list clears what the package inherits.

ignore-dependencies.description: Replaces the ignored dependencies; an empty list clears what the package inherits.

ignore-binaries.description: Replaces the ignored binaries; an empty list clears what the package inherits.

ignore-unresolved.description: Replaces the ignored unresolved specifiers; an empty list clears what the package inherits.

extend-ignore-unresolved.description: Appended to the ignored unresolved specifiers.

plugins.description: Plugin switches and options for the selected packages.

PackageJs.description:
`[js]` keys an override can set for the packages it selects.

Globs are relative to each selected package. The `extend-*` keys append to what the package inherits; the others
replace it, and set to an empty list they clear it.
